evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Multi-function Dictionary), character entry 最
evidence.field: 形義通解; 《說文》; 《廣韻》; character form tables
evidence.text: The entry repeats the Shuowen account 「犯而取也。从冃从取」 and explains it as “to offend/force one’s way and take.” It lists the 《廣韻》 fanqie 祖外 and Middle Chinese category 精母、泰韻、合口一等. Its form table displays a seal-script form, but no bronze or oracle forms; the page does not substantiate the dossier’s proposed early 㝡 form or claim that distinguishing marks were added. Treat the Shuowen component analysis as a historical explanation, not independent proof that 冃 and 取 function respectively as semantic and phonetic components.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Multi-function Dictionary), character entry 最
evidence.field: 形義通解; dated textual examples
evidence.text: The entry separates later attested uses: 《漢書·宣帝紀》 has 最 in the administrative ranking expression 課殿最; 《燕丹子》 uses it for a foremost person or thing; 《小爾雅·廣詁》 glosses 最 as 要 (“summary/essential”); 《管子·禁藏》 uses it in a context glossed by the commentator as 聚 (“gather”); 《史記·絳侯周勃世家》 has a totaling sense; and 《墨子·經上》 uses 最 as “foremost.” The page also cites a Tang poem for a “just/exactly” adverbial use. These examples show distinct uses, but the page supplies no first-attestation chronology for the modern superlative sense; gloss order must not be read as chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Multi-function Dictionary), character entry 取
evidence.field: 形義通解; character form tables
evidence.text: The entry describes oracle-bone and bronze forms of 取 as 耳 plus 又, interpreted as a hand holding an ear, with a basic sense of taking/holding. It reports oracle-bone uses meaning obtain (examples 取牛, 取馬), and bronze uses including take, receive, and select. This supports 取’s independent history as a graph for “take/obtain,” but does not by itself establish that it is phonetic in 最.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, entry A00302-005
evidence.field: research explanation for 㝡 as a variant of 最
evidence.text: The entry identifies 㝡 as a nonstandard variant of 最, citing the Sui Longzangsi stele, Qianlu zishu, Dunhuang popular forms, and Duan Yucai’s note that 㝡 was used in the Six Dynasties. It cites Guangyun’s gloss 最，極也 (“utmost”) and says 㝡 was a common form in that period. This is evidence for a later variant relationship, not evidence that 㝡 is the original form from which 最 developed.
evidence.title: [A00302-005] (最) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, entry A00302
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes several variant histories. It says a form written with 曰 above 取 results from 冃 being misread or written as 曰; it treats 冣 as a distinct graph in Shuowen meaning “accumulate,” later used as a variant of 最; and it reports a separate hole-top variant as an unexplained graphic corruption. These accounts caution against collapsing distinct variants or treating every 曰/冖/穴 form as evidence for the original structure of 最.
evidence.title: [A00302] 最 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

gaps: No accessible inspected paleographic source established a pre-Han original graphic for 最, an original 㝡 form, or the claim that two marks were later added. The inspected character page displays seal script but no bronze/oracle forms.

The source-based graphic accounts conflict: Shuowen analyzes 冃 + 取 as “offend/force one’s way and take”; the dossier’s phonosemantic analysis calls 取 phonetic; variant dictionaries describe later variant/corruption relations. The researched evidence does not resolve whether 最 is ideographic or phonosemantic, and does not demonstrate that 取’s independent “take” word was borrowed as a whole graph for “most.”

The relevant Baxter–Sagart PDF was located but browser opening failed with 502. Local exact Baxter–Sagart row for 最 is *[ts]ˤot-s; no exact row for 取 was supplied, so historical sound comparison of the proposed component is unresolved. Do not reproduce a secondary transcription for 取 as though it were checked.

Per-character official Unihan URLs for 最, 取, and 㝡 were attempted but inaccessible. The local exact kMandarin rows for 最 and 㝡 are zuì; no 取 row was provided. Unicode documentation establishes the field’s nature but not these exact per-character readings.

The cited source provides classical examples across senses but does not establish a complete first-attestation sequence for “most,” “extremely,” “gather,” or “total.” The semantic links among gathering, ranking/superlative, summary, and adverbial use remain unproven here.
The local manifest's Wikimedia seal glyph lead was not opened or visually inspected; no claim is made about that image, its provenance, or its dating.

The accessible sources do not establish a pre-Han original graphic form for 最, a graphic sequence from an original 㝡 form, or a theory that distinguishing marks were added later. The Ministry of Education page lists early-form resources for 最 as unpublished; the inspected character entry supplies a seal form only.

The traditional Shuowen account parses 冃 + 取 as a meaning-based phrase (“offend/force one’s way and take”). Other dossier sources propose a phonosemantic analysis with 取 as sound. No inspected primary paleographic evidence resolves these competing analyses. Similarities in Baxter–Sagart reconstructions are relevant comparison data, not proof of phonetic function.

The proposed explanation that a whole 取 graph was borrowed for 最’s superlative meaning is not demonstrated. Evidence for 取’s independent “take” word and graph does not itself establish whole-graph borrowing.

Cited sources give examples of different senses but no securely ordered first attestations for the modern superlative “most,” “extremely,” “gather,” ranking, summary, or total. Semantic links among those uses remain undemonstrated; dictionary gloss order is not chronology.

Official Unihan per-character endpoints for 最 and 取 could not be opened. The exact current kMandarin readings are preserved from local rows, while Unicode’s general lookup interface is cited only for the kind of data its database supplies.

Commons glyphs are digital redrawings in Shuowen seal-script style rather than artifact photographs. The 最 SVG has explicit Sinica source and CC0 statement.
